key_insight: C-MIG improves clinical diagnosis reasoning by using multi-view information gain rewards that better capture semantically relevant evidence and supervise different parts of the retrieval-and-refinement process.
clinical_relevance: This could help retrieval-augmented clinical AI produce more reliable, evidence-grounded diagnostic support with better recall of medically relevant information.
method: Estimates information gain with a frozen reference model from two views: retrieved-document and document-refinement.
Uses those signals to guide both what to retrieve and how to refine the retrieved evidence.
Adds a multi-subquery retrieval strategy to increase knowledge coverage in clinical diagnosis tasks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong results on four medical benchmarks, with C-MIG outperforming other RAG-RL methods on in-domain and out-of-domain sets and surpassing state-of-the-art general-purpose LLMs.
watch_item: Performance is benchmark-based, so real-world clinical deployment would still need careful validation for safety, generalization, and evidence traceability.
paper_title: C-MIG: Multi-view Information Gain-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Clinical Diagnosis Reasoning
